column1: Slug|Meaning|Sequence|Practice|Caution

ai-agents|Build goal-directed systems that use tools and environmental feedback while remaining within explicit authority.|Single model call; fixed workflow; validated tools; durable state; bounded agent loop; task evaluation and operations|Build a read-only investigation agent, then demonstrate its stopping, permission, and recovery behavior.|More autonomous steps create more opportunities for compounded errors; autonomy needs measured justification.

ai-engineer|Build useful model-backed software by combining model capabilities with data, evaluation, and reliable application boundaries.|Programming and APIs; model behavior; prompting and context; retrieval; evaluation; deployment and monitoring|Ship a cited-answer service with a held-out evaluation set and measured latency and cost.|A model benchmark score does not establish that a customer workflow is safe or useful.

ai-product-builder|Turn a validated user problem into an AI-enabled product with observable customer value.|Problem discovery; workflow prototype; model and data feasibility; pilot; adoption and economics; product iteration|Test a narrow operator workflow with real acceptance criteria and a clear stop decision.|Do not equate generated features or a successful demo with repeated customer value.

api-design|Define understandable, stable, secure contracts between clients and services.|Resource and operation design; schemas and errors; identity and authorization; pagination; idempotency; evolution and documentation|Specify and test a job API with explicit accepted, running, failed, and completed states.|A syntactically valid request still needs object authorization and business-rule validation.

aws|Operate a coherent cloud system using AWS identity, networking, compute, storage, and managed services.|Account boundaries and IAM; networking; compute and storage; application deployment; monitoring; cost and recovery|Deploy a sandbox service with scoped workload identity, private data, telemetry, and a restore exercise.|Avoid administrator credentials and unnecessary services; confirm region, quotas, data policy, and recurring cost.

backend|Enforce domain rules, persistent state, authorization, and integration reliability behind user-facing applications.|Language and runtime; HTTP and APIs; relational data; authorization; queues and integration; testing and operations|Build a multi-tenant ticket API with an asynchronous enrichment job and replay-safe updates.|Authentication alone is not authorization, and successful transport is not completed business work.

claude-code|Use a coding agent with clear context, permissions, review, and executable acceptance evidence.|Tool setup and policy; repository context; scoped tasks; permissions; diff review; tests and recovery|Fix one defect in a sandbox repository and explain every changed file and validation result.|Tool and model capabilities change; inspect current vendor settings rather than assuming broad terminal authority is necessary.

cpp|Work with native components where ownership, interoperability, or measured performance justifies C++.|Language basics; object lifetime and RAII; standard containers; build tooling; tests and sanitizers; profiling|Inspect a native data-processing or inference boundary and test buffer ownership and error propagation.|Do not modify native boundaries without understanding lifetime, ABI compatibility, and cleanup behavior.

css|Design robust visual layouts that remain usable under real content, viewport, zoom, and accessibility conditions.|Cascade and box model; layout primitives; responsive constraints; interaction states; accessibility; maintainable styling|Style an operator dashboard with long names, failures, empty states, and narrow screens.|A layout that works with placeholder content at one resolution is not a validated interface.

cyber-security|Protect systems through threat modeling, secure architecture, technical controls, detection, and response.|Systems and networks; identity; application security; infrastructure controls; detection; incident response and governance|Threat-model the capstone and prove that sensitive boundaries resist unauthorized access and unsafe effects.|Operate only in authorized environments; security learning does not authorize testing a third party's systems.

data-engineer|Produce trustworthy, traceable data for applications and analytics across ingestion, transformation, and serving.|SQL and modeling; source audits; batch and streaming; orchestration; quality and lineage; serving and operations|Build a pipeline that handles duplicates, late data, failed batches, correction, and replay.|Unreliable identifiers, permissions, and event time can invalidate downstream AI work before modeling begins.

datastructures-and-algorithms|Choose data structures and algorithms by correctness, complexity, and the shape of the problem.|Arrays and maps; stacks and queues; recursion; trees and graphs; sorting and searching; complexity and patterns|Implement ticket deduplication and dependency traversal with tests and time and space analysis.|Recognizing a memorized pattern is not enough; defend invariants and behavior on edge cases.

devops|Connect reproducible implementation, release, operation, and feedback through explicit ownership and automation.|Linux and networking; version control; CI and artifacts; configuration; deployment; telemetry and recovery|Create a tested release pipeline with an artifact manifest and rehearsed rollback or roll-forward.|Automating a release does not make its migrations, permissions, or operational handover correct.

devsecops|Integrate security policy, evidence, and controls into development and delivery.|Threat model; code and dependency checks; identity and secrets; infrastructure policy; artifact provenance; exceptions and response|Add scoped CI identity, secret checking, and an expiring risk-exception process to a delivery pipeline.|A clean scanner result does not certify the system; unresolved risk needs a named owner and decision.

docker|Package and run applications as reproducible images with deliberate runtime boundaries.|Images and layers; Dockerfiles; builds; configuration; storage and networking; runtime policy and observability|Build and inspect an image, then test non-root execution, health behavior, shutdown, and secret handling.|Secrets can remain in image history, and a container is not equivalent to a fully isolated trusted machine.

frontend|Build interfaces that let users complete tasks with understandable state and failure recovery.|Semantic HTML; CSS; JavaScript; component and state design; API integration; accessibility and testing|Build the capstone review screen with citations, correction controls, and explicit loading and error states.|Measure task completion and accessibility, not only visual similarity to a mockup.

full-stack|Deliver a vertical slice across interface, API, identity, persistence, and deployment.|User flow; browser interface; service contract; data model; authorization; release and monitoring|Ship a ticket investigation workflow end to end with one tested failure and one recovery path.|Avoid learning every framework simultaneously; own a small coherent stack and its operational behavior.

git-github|Make changes reviewable, reproducible, collaborative, and recoverable through version control.|Repository basics; commits and history; branching; merges and conflicts; review; automation and release tagging|Deliver a feature through a reviewable change with tests and a clear recovery description.|Do not store credentials in source history or accept a merge without reviewing its behavior and deployment impact.

golang|Build deployable Go services and infrastructure tools with explicit errors, resource ownership, and cancellation.|Language and modules; interfaces; errors; HTTP; concurrency and context; testing and profiling|Implement a bounded concurrent resource checker with deadlines and deterministic fixture tests.|Unbounded goroutines, missing cancellation, and ignored errors can turn a small tool into an operational problem.

graphql|Expose typed client-selected data while retaining server responsibility for authorization and cost.|Schemas and resolvers; queries and mutations; pagination; object access; batching; evolution and complexity limits|Expose tickets and events with a paginated query and test nested cross-tenant access.|Schema types do not prevent N+1 calls, expensive queries, or unauthorized object traversal.

html|Give documents and controls the structure and native semantics needed by browsers and assistive technology.|Document structure; headings and landmarks; links and forms; tables; media alternatives; validation and accessibility|Create a usable ticket-review form and evidence table before styling them.|Native elements provide behavior that must otherwise be reimplemented and tested for every custom control.

inference-engineering|Run model inference within measurable quality, latency, throughput, memory, reliability, and cost budgets.|Workload characterization; prefill and decode; serving and concurrency; memory and caching; optimization; operational measurement|Benchmark an inference workload at representative concurrency and test one optimization against unchanged quality cases.|Tokens per second alone does not describe user latency; queueing and retrieval may dominate.

java|Work with JVM services and libraries using explicit contracts, established tooling, and operational understanding.|Language and collections; objects and interfaces; errors; build tooling; concurrency; services and tests|Extend a small Java adapter with validated inputs, a focused test, and documented runtime settings.|Do not introduce a framework or runtime upgrade without examining customer compatibility and operational ownership.

javascript|Understand browser and server JavaScript behavior around modules, asynchronous work, events, and data.|Language semantics; collections and functions; modules; promises; DOM or runtime APIs; testing and tooling|Build cancellable search that prevents older responses from replacing newer results.|Syntactic familiarity does not prevent stale state, unhandled rejection, or accidental event-loop blocking.

kubernetes|Operate container workloads through declarative scheduling, service discovery, identity, and controlled rollouts.|Pods and deployments; services and networking; configuration; storage; probes and resources; access and troubleshooting|Deploy a sandbox service, induce a failed readiness check, and recover a bad rollout.|Use Kubernetes only when the environment warrants its operational complexity; probe design can cause failure loops.

linux|Inspect and operate deployed systems through files, permissions, processes, networking, services, and logs.|Shell navigation; permissions; processes and signals; networking; services; storage and troubleshooting|Diagnose a service with a bad permission, missing configuration, or unreachable dependency.|Avoid escalating privileges or exposing secrets before understanding the failure.

mlops|Control the lifecycle of model-related data, artifacts, release, monitoring, and change.|Data and experiment lineage; artifact versioning; testing; serving; monitoring; retraining or adaptation triggers|Create a release manifest tying application, model, prompt, evaluator, embedding, and index versions together.|Versioning weights alone does not explain changing data, prompts, retrieval, or scoring behavior.

mongodb|Use document-oriented storage with explicit access patterns, schema expectations, indexing, and consistency needs.|Document modeling; CRUD and queries; validation; indexes; aggregation; replication, backup, and operational limits|Model ticket snapshots and query their history while documenting duplication and update behavior.|Flexible schema does not remove the need for invariants, migration, validation, and access controls.

nodejs|Build I/O-oriented JavaScript services with explicit lifecycle, asynchronous control, and bounded resource use.|Runtime and modules; event loop; HTTP; streams; persistence; errors, tests, and operation|Stream and validate an upload while keeping concurrent API requests responsive.|CPU-heavy work and unbounded buffering can block or exhaust the request-serving process.

openclaw|Assess and operate the particular OpenClaw agent deployment with explicit integrations, identities, and safety controls.|Verify project and version; sandbox setup; integrations; permissions; audit; shutdown and recovery|Prepare a restricted pilot and document every data destination and permission before enabling integrations.|Brand familiarity or a tutorial is not evidence that broad workspace or enterprise permissions are safe.

postgresql-dba|Design and operate PostgreSQL with attention to integrity, concurrency, performance, migration, and recovery.|Schema and constraints; transactions; indexes and plans; permissions; backup and restore; monitoring and maintenance|Create constrained ticket and event tables, measure representative queries, and restore a backup separately.|A backup that has not been restored is incomplete recovery evidence; transactions still require appropriate isolation.

prompt-engineering|Specify tasks and output expectations through testable instructions, examples, and clear data boundaries.|Task contract; instructions versus data; examples; output schema; abstention; evaluation and versioning|Evaluate an extraction prompt against missing, conflicting, malformed, and adversarial inputs.|Repeated anecdotal prompt edits can introduce contradictions and overfit the examples being used to certify quality.

python|Build maintainable data and application tooling with explicit dependencies, errors, boundaries, and tests.|Language and collections; modules and environments; file and network I/O; validation; services; testing and packaging|Build a reproducible ingestion command and API using synthetic fixtures and bounded network retries.|Notebook hidden state and broad exception handling can hide defects that appear in a fresh deployment.

react|Express a task-oriented interface as components with deliberate state ownership and explicit data flow.|Components and props; state; events and forms; effects; server interaction; accessibility and behavior tests|Build ticket filtering and draft review while preserving edits and rejecting stale request updates.|Do not store multiple competing copies of derived state or use effects to compensate for unclear state ownership.

redis|Use in-memory data structures with an explicit understanding of persistence, expiry, consistency, and failure.|Data types and commands; keys and TTL; caching patterns; persistence; replication; memory and access controls|Add a ticket metadata cache and test expiry, invalidation, cache miss, and Redis outage behavior.|A cache is not automatically a durable source of truth, and stale permissions can become a data-exposure defect.

rust|Use ownership and types to build safe systems components where the tradeoff is justified.|Ownership and borrowing; enums and traits; Result and Option; collections; I/O; tests and profiling|Build a streaming validation utility and demonstrate safe handling of malformed input and cleanup.|Avoid unnecessary unsafe code or a language migration without a measured or maintenance-driven reason.

scala|Work with Scala and JVM data systems while understanding their type, runtime, and execution behavior.|Language and collections; functional abstractions; JVM tooling; effects and errors; concurrency; Spark where needed|Extend a small Scala data transformation and explain its errors, dependencies, and execution assumptions.|Concise transformations can conceal expensive distributed work or abstractions the team cannot maintain.

shell-bash|Compose repeatable command-line operations with correct quoting, exit behavior, and resource boundaries.|Shell evaluation; quoting and variables; streams and pipes; conditions; functions and scripts; safe error handling|Write a sandbox log-audit command that handles spaces, failed commands, missing files, and large inputs.|An unquoted expansion or ignored exit status can make a harmless-looking automation unreliable or destructive.

sql|Query and transform relational data with an explicit row grain, NULL behavior, and transaction model.|Selection and filtering; joins; aggregation; subqueries and windows; transactions; plans and indexing|Calculate a support metric and reconcile it against a hand-checked sample after joining event history.|One-to-many joins can silently multiply rows and invalidate business conclusions.

system-design|Allocate computation, data, and responsibility across components under explicit scale and failure constraints.|Requirements and estimates; interfaces and data; caching and queues; consistency; resilience; observability and tradeoffs|Design ticket ingestion with a capacity estimate, first bottleneck, retry contract, and recovery plan.|Do not substitute a collection of fashionable services for a design tied to actual constraints.

technical-writer|Produce documentation that enables a specific reader to complete a specific task and recover from failure.|Audience and task; structure and terminology; examples; reference contracts; review; maintenance|Have an unfamiliar engineer follow your setup guide and outage runbook without verbal assistance.|Documentation of intended behavior is insufficient without prerequisites, verification, and recovery guidance.

terraform|Manage infrastructure changes as reviewed plans against protected state and explicit lifecycle rules.|Providers and configuration; resources and dependencies; state and locking; modules; environments; drift and change review|Review a plan that replaces a stateful resource and document data preservation and recovery.|State can contain sensitive values; a plan does not guarantee that destructive changes are reversible.

typescript|Add static contracts to JavaScript while preserving validation at untrusted runtime boundaries.|Types and inference; unions and narrowing; generics; modules; compiler settings; boundary validation|Create a strict typed API client that rejects malformed responses and handles explicit error variants.|Type annotations disappear at runtime and cannot prove that an external payload or permission claim is valid.

vibe-coding|Use AI-assisted development while retaining human responsibility for requirements, code review, testing, and security.|Define acceptance behavior; provide scoped context; inspect changes; run checks; review dependencies and access; deploy deliberately|Implement one small feature with an assistant and explain both the diff and regression evidence.|A single successful run does not establish correctness, maintainability, or safe data access.
